review_basis:
A genuinely fresh real project (West Valley College STEM Classroom HVAC, California), pulled from the corpus_2 GitHub Release during the same low-intensity corpus-hunting pass as e2508-gas-m103.json/ochc-chwsr-m102.json/poultry-ra-m101.json. Screened for image coverage first per Run 86's own established check: `imgRatio` reads ~0.01 on sheet M201, real vector CAD, safe to sweep.

This sheet's 236 real size-callout text spans are overwhelmingly `(E)`-prefixed (an existing-marker printed BEFORE the whole label, e.g. `(E) 6"ø`, `(E)10"ø`) -- a known, already-catalogued grammar gap (a structural prefix change, not a suffix fix like the ones already made this session) that is deliberately NOT touched this pass. Instead this golden targets one of the sheet's few non-`(E)`-prefixed labels, which parses cleanly with the existing grammar: a bare `22"x12"` rectangular duct callout with no leading system token.

A grid sweep of this and eleven other non-`(E)` labels on the sheet found one confirmed hatching-mistrace pathology on a different candidate (5332 LF, cap/cap, 3998 vertices -- rejected, matching the established pattern from prior runs) and this real, automatic-bind-capable short candidate. `trace_run` returns a real 3.39 LF two-segment run through a real 117.3-degree elbow: `size:{kind:rect,w_in:22,h_in:12}`, factors `["stroke-family:pen-weight-prior","size-binding:beside","ambiguous_stop","layer-unclassified","scale_unconfirmed"]`, confidence 0.5. A wide marked crop confirms the run visually: the `22"x12"` label's own leader terminates at the forward `dead_end` stop; the backward `ambiguous` stop (a real 4-candidate fan in the raw `trace_run` response) sits at a duct-collar connection into fan coil unit FC-A (tag "5"), from which the run continues (out of scope) as a trunk feeding several `(E)`-prefixed round branch ducts (6"/8"/10" diameter) that in turn feed CFM-tagged supply diffusers in the adjacent OFFICE rooms (A110/A111/A121/A122). A `resolveRunSegments` recompute from the authored vertices reproduces the identical two segments (2.76 LF + 0.63 LF = 3.39 LF total, matching `totals_by_size`) and a reseed `trace_run` from a fresh coordinate against the freshly re-loaded, already-committed raw PDF reproduces identical points, length, and size.

Honest caveat on the `system` field: this sheet carries no explicit system-letter prefix on the `22"x12"` callout itself (unlike this session's other multi/single-system goldens). "SA" (supply air) is inferred from the run's own topology -- an unmarked (i.e., new, non-`(E)`) rectangular main duct running directly off fan coil unit FC-A and branching into round ducts that feed CFM-labeled supply diffusers in adjacent offices, a standard fan-coil-to-diffuser supply arrangement -- rather than read directly off a label. A sheet-wide text search for an explicit FC-A supply/return schedule or legend on this sheet found only generic project notes (fan coil general notes, an unrelated FC-A-#-# equipment tag list) with no line-by-line SA/RA legend to confirm this specific duct run. Per this corpus's established convention (see ochc-chwsr-m102.json), `run.system` is documentation only and never affects `sizeMatch` scoring, so this uncertainty does not affect any GATE 3 metric, but it is disclosed here rather than asserted as confirmed.
scope: A single real 22x12-inch rectangular duct segment (3.39 LF) on the West Valley College STEM Classroom HVAC project's own mechanical plan, sheet M201, from a real duct-collar connection at fan coil unit FC-A (tag "5") through a real 117.3-degree elbow to the label's own leader terminus. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the run's own continuation past the equipment connection (the other three candidate directions at that real multi-candidate junction, including the round branch ducts FC-A feeds onward to office diffusers); every `(E)`-prefixed round duct on this same sheet (dozens, not attempted this pass, blocked on the parenthetical-prefix grammar gap); the rejected 5332 LF hatching-mistrace candidate found during the same sweep; every other sheet on this real project's plan set.
